title: Vector Dimensionality Shrink/Grow Migration Checklist and Client Compatibility Notes
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Goal: safely change embedding vector dimensionality for a set of catalog models (both shrink and expand scenarios) while minimizing client disruptions, preserving reranker quality, and keeping query latency and index rebuild costs bounded. This ticket captures an actionable checklist and notes for SDK teams, runtime rollout, and reindex jobs. Scope includes: schema versioning, on-disk index format changes, realtime/online reindex vs offline bulk reindex, client-side adapters (pad/truncate), and signal validation for rerankers that depend on vector norm or dimensional features.
acceptance_criteria: Clients using latest SDK receive clear dimensionality metadata and can opt-in to automated adapters.
Online reindex process completes for 10M vectors in <48h at target cluster size with documented throughput tuning knobs.
Reranker quality regression measured on canonical eval set within ±1% NDCG for both shrink and expand cases.
Query latency P95 increase <= 10ms and P99 increase <= 20ms for embedding-powered endpoints during migration windows.
Rollback path validated: alias swap reverts to previous index within 5 minutes and no loss of traffic routing or auth state.
migration_steps: Publish embedding schema v2 with 'dim' and 'base_model' metadata fields in model catalog and runtime responses.
Release SDK adapter patch (js/py/go) that reads schema dim; if incoming vectors mismatch, apply configurable pad/truncate or reject with 422 and guidance URL.
Dual-write mode: during initial rollout, accept both v1 and v2 embeddings on write endpoints and tag index entries with schema version.
Backfill strategy: start with low-priority background workers to reindex cold partitions; run hot-partition reindex during maintenance windows with throttling via autoscaler target concurrency.
Index swap: build new index (v2) in parallel and use routing alias to swap when health checks pass; keep old index for 7 days before GC.
KV cache handling: on-disk cache invalidation policy to ensure previous token-level caches that include embedded-sized blobs are invalidated when schema changes; add cache version header.
Reranker recalibration: retrain or retune reranker calibration layers (if present) on v2 embeddings or add a small mapping layer (linear projection) as temporary shim.
Monitoring: create migration dashboard showing reindex progress, per-shard throughput, query latency deltas, and rerank quality metrics per rollout cohort.
rollout_plan: Week 0: announce migration timeline and SDK compatibility changes, feature-flag SDK adapter. Week 1: enable dual-write and start background backfills for least-accessed partitions. Week 2: promote reindex for medium-traffic partitions with concurrency ramping. Week 3: index swap for low-risk customers and monitor; Week 4: full migration for remaining customers, enable automatic pad/truncate in SDKs unless customer opts-out. Communicate deprecation of v1 schema with 30-day notice after full migration.
rollback_plan: If quality regressions or latency > threshold observed, revert routing alias to previous index, disable pad/truncate auto-adapter in SDKs, and mark migration as paused. Keep audit logs and reindex checkpoints to resume. Post-mortem and follow-up action items required before reattempt.
performance_considerations: Batch size for reindex workers empirically impacts DMA throughput and peak memory — default to 512 vectors per batch and increase only after load testing.
Use quantized storage (int8/4bit) for archive index copies to reduce IO and speed rebuilds, but validate downstream reranker accepts quantized inputs or add dequant layer.
Network egress for large reindexes: use within-region S3/Blob stores and local ETL nodes to avoid cross-region costs and latency spikes.
Estimate incremental CPU/GPU for on-the-fly projection shims in rerankers to avoid blocking inference pipelines.
client_compatibility_notes: SDKs will expose embedding.dim in model metadata; clients should not hardcode dimension numbers.
Adapter behavior: 'pad' mode fills trailing zeros and 'truncate' removes trailing dims; 'strict' mode returns 422 with migration guidance link.
For reranking clients that compute cosine similarity, we recommend clients normalize vectors after adapter pad/truncate to avoid norm drift.
Backward compatibility: server will accept v1 vectors if tagged as 'schema:v1' for 30 days; recommend clients upgrade within the deprecation window.
Large customers with custom rerankers should be offered a 'compatibility audit' where we run a small A/B rerank comparison and provide a projection matrix if needed.
test_plan: Synthetic soak test: 72h of mixed query+index load with production-shaped distribution and embedded-dimensionality toggles.
Quality eval: run canonical reranking NDCG and MRR suites comparing v1 vs v2 for at least 5 representative datasets (search, chat, summarization).
Latency regression: automated canary runs during reindex with 1% traffic for 48h, capturing P50/P95/P99 and CPU/GPU saturation metrics.
SDK integration tests: dimension negotiation tests covering pad/truncate/strict modes and error paths.
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert if reindex worker error rate > 0.5% for 15m.
Alert if query P99 latency increases > 20ms compared to baseline for 10m.
Alert if reranker NDCG drops > 1.5% on canonical eval cohort after index swap.
Dashboard panels: reindex progress, per-shard queue depth, pad/truncate adapter usage, client upgrade adoption rate.
notes: Open questions: exact GC window for old indices (currently 7 days), whether to support automatic projection layers in hosted runtime permanently, and pricing implications for prolonged dual-write. Next step: tech review with SDK leads and infra (scheduled 2025-02-22).
